You are grading an AI assistant's answer to a question about a company handbook.

Question: What swag item can a GitLab employee receive on their five‑year anniversary?
Reference answer (written from the handbook): They can receive a GitLab branded computer backpack.

Passages the assistant was given:
"""
[New Hires, Celebrations and Significant Life Events > New Hire Swag > Celebrations > GitLab Anniversary > Anniversary Gifts]
Team members celebrating a GitLab anniversary will have the option to select a custom swag item only available to those celebrating an anniversary. Team members celebrating their one-year anniversary have the option to receive a custom GitLab Tech-Caddy. Those celebrating their three-year anniversary have the option of a branded 3-piece tumbler, pen and notebook set. Folks celebrating their five-year anniversary have the option of a GitLab branded computer backpack. And finally, team members celebrating their tenth-year anniversary have the option of receiving a custom swag package.

No action is required by team members in order to receive these gifts! If you are due an anniversary gift the vendor team, Brilliant, will email you on the day of your anniversary with a specific redemption link. The People Operations team runs a monthly report from Workday during the first week of the new month looking back to the previous month to audit the eligible team members and makes sure all emails were sent out.

[New Hires, Celebrations and Significant Life Events > New Hire Swag > Celebrations > GitLab Anniversary]
At GitLab we like to acknowledge and celebrate team member milestones and contributions. This means that those celebrating their first, third, fifth and tenth hire-date anniversary will receive a token of acknowledgement.

Along with this, all celebrants regardless of length of tenure will receive a mention in the **#team-member-updates** channel which allows the greater GitLab community to share in the celebration!

[New Hires, Celebrations and Significant Life Events > New Hire Swag > Celebrations > GitLab Anniversary > Redeeming New Hire Swag and Anniversary Swag]
Please note: the New Hire and Anniversary Swag links are provided specifically for the redemption of preselected items. These items are not eligible for exchange or conversion to swag shop credit.

If you have any questions or need further assistance regarding New Hire or Anniversary Swag, please don't hesitate to reach out to the People Operations team through [Compass](https://app.serval.com/new-request).

[New Hires, Celebrations and Significant Life Events > New Hire Swag > New Parent Swag]
Welcoming a new child into your family is an exciting life event that GitLab wants to help celebrate. New parents will receive a swag bundle that includes a teething ring, baby socks, plush tag blanket, adult socks, baby bib and baby blanket (all GitLab branded). The Absence Management team will mail the gift to the team member. There is no action required by the team member or their manager. Gifts are ordered on a weekly cadence, although time to ship and customs can vary depending on the country. For questions related to new parent swag, please email leaves@gitlab.com.

[Incentives at GitLab > Compensation for Acting and Interim Roles > Referral Bonuses > GitLab Anniversaries]
At 10:00 UTC on Thursday of every week, `PeopleOps Bot` slack bot will send a shout out on the `#team-member-updates` channel congratulating all team members who celebrates a hire date anniversary that week.
Visit our [GitLab Anniversary Gift](/handbook/people-group/celebrations/#anniversary-gifts) section for more information about the gifts.

[New Hires, Celebrations and Significant Life Events > New Hire Swag]
As a new hire at GitLab, you will be getting a customized welcome package! On your date of hire you will receive an [email](https://internal.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/people-operations/people-operations/onboarding_process/#new-hire-swag-email) to claim the package with a redemption link. Then simply enter your shipping information to have your welcome swag shipped directly to you.
"""

Assistant's answer:
"""
Team members celebrating their five-year anniversary have the option of a GitLab branded computer backpack [1].
"""

First write one sentence of reasoning, then grade three things:
- correctness: "correct" if the answer states the key information in the reference answer without contradicting it (extra correct detail is fine); "partial" if it gets part of it or is vague; "incorrect" if it is wrong, contradicts the reference, or does not answer.
- refused: true if the assistant declined or said it does not know, instead of answering.
- faithful: true if every factual claim in the answer is supported by the passages above (ignore whether it matches the reference). An answer that only refuses counts as faithful.
The grades must agree with your reasoning.
Return JSON with the reasoning first: {"reason": "one sentence", "correctness": "correct" | "partial" | "incorrect", "refused": true/false, "faithful": true/false}
